name: Kinetic Motion Charger
what: Harvests the energy of walking or shaking to keep small devices topped up without a plug.
how: A moving magnet or rotor inside a coil induces current as you move — the same principle as an automatic watch.

how: A carbon-14 diamond betavoltaic cell trickles microwatts to a low-power sensor and radio — sealed and maintenance-free.

how: Flexible printed electronics conform to skin, sensing temperature, strain and biomarkers, powered by body heat or motion.
whatItIs: A stretchy, skin-thin patch of sensors that reads vitals, sweat chemistry and motion continuously.

name: Home Backup Battery
use: Blackout backup, solar self-consumption, peak-tariff shifting
what: A wall- or floor-mounted battery that stores household electricity and runs the house when the grid drops or power is expensive.
how: Lithium iron phosphate cells sit behind a hybrid inverter that decides moment to moment whether to charge from solar, discharge to the house, or pass grid power through.

name: Learning Smart Thermostat
use: Heating and cooling control, scheduling, energy reporting
what: A thermostat that learns when a home is occupied and stops heating or cooling empty rooms, which is where most wasted household energy goes.
how: Occupancy and temperature sensors build a schedule the unit follows on its own, and it talks to the heating system over a standard low-voltage or wireless control link.

name: Bidirectional EV Charger
use: Vehicle-to-home backup, tariff arbitrage, grid export
what: A charger that lets an electric car push power back out, turning the vehicle's battery into the largest energy store most households will ever own.
how: The wallbox converts between the car's DC pack and household AC in both directions, with an interlock that disconnects from the grid before running the house islanded.

name: AI Mini PC
use: Running language models offline, private inference, small-team AI
what: A desktop box built so a language model runs entirely on your own hardware, with nothing sent to a provider.
how: A large pool of unified memory shared between CPU and integrated GPU lets a big quantised model stay resident, which matters far more for local inference than the advertised NPU figure.

name: AI Note-Taking Recorder
what: A pocket recorder that turns what it hears into a transcript and a summary without you typing anything up afterwards.
how: On-device capture is paired with speech-to-text and a summarising model, usually in the cloud, so recording quality and consent handling matter more than the hardware.

name: AI Navigation Robot Vacuum
use: Whole-home floor cleaning, pet households, mopping
what: A floor robot that recognises what it is looking at, so it drives around cables and pet mess instead of dragging them through the house.
how: A laser scanner builds the room map while a small vision model running on the robot classifies obstacles in its path, and the dock empties and washes it between runs.

name: Matter Smart Home Hub
use: Cross-brand automation, local control, Thread networking
what: The box that lets smart devices from different brands work as one system instead of needing an app each.
how: It speaks the Matter standard and acts as a Thread border router, bridging a low-power mesh of sensors and locks onto the home network so automations keep running without the internet.

name: Self-Fitting Hearing Aid Earbuds
use: Mild to moderate hearing loss, conversation in noise
what: Earbuds sold directly to the wearer that are tuned by a hearing test taken on your own phone, with no clinic visit in between.
how: An in-app tone test builds a personal hearing profile, and the buds apply that gain curve per frequency band while separating speech from background noise.

name: Sleep Apnoea Detection Wearable
what: A watch or band that flags the repeated breathing interruptions of sleep apnoea, a condition most people who have it have never been tested for.
how: Blood-oxygen and movement sensors look for the pattern of oxygen dips and micro-arousals across a night, and report a risk signal rather than a diagnosis.

name: Cuffless Blood Pressure Monitor
what: A wrist device that estimates blood pressure without inflating a cuff, so readings can be taken through the day rather than once at a clinic.
how: Optical and pressure sensors time the pulse waveform at the wrist and infer pressure from it, which is why these devices still need periodic calibration against a real cuff.

name: Indoor Air Quality Monitor
use: Ventilation checks, allergy management, damp and mould risk
what: A desk or wall sensor that shows what the air indoors is actually carrying, which is otherwise invisible until it affects someone.
how: A laser particle counter sizes airborne dust while separate sensors read carbon dioxide, humidity and volatile organic compounds, and the CO2 reading is the one that tracks ventilation.

name: Neural Input Wristband
use: Hands-free control, accessibility input, wearable interfaces
what: A wristband that reads the nerve signals heading to your hand, so a barely-formed finger movement becomes an input.
how: Surface electromyography electrodes pick up motor-unit activity at the forearm and a model decodes intended gestures before the hand visibly moves.

name: Open-Hardware Handheld Computer
what: A pocket computer whose schematics and firmware are published, built for people who want to repair and change it rather than replace it.
how: Off-the-shelf ARM or RISC-V modules are mounted on an openly documented mainboard running mainline Linux, so parts and drivers stay obtainable after the campaign ends.

name: Personal AI Health Sentinel
what: A continuous blood-chemistry monitor that predicts illness before symptoms appear.
how: Uses interstitial fluid sensing and AI pattern matching against a global health database.

name: Quantum Encryption Key-Fob
what: A hardware wallet that generates truly random quantum keys for unbreakable communication.
how: Leverages photon polarization states to create non-deterministic cryptographic seeds.
